html_body:

No positions to review today. The story is three unfilled buy orders sitting since Tuesday with no stop legs — see below.

⚠️ Decisions needed — 3 pending orders, 2 days stale

AXTI (2 sh @ $58 limit), SPXC (0.5 sh @ $200 limit), and GOOG (0.3 sh @ $365 limit) have all been sitting unfilled as GTC orders since Aug 4 — none have a stop-limit leg attached. If they fill unattended you'd own three fresh positions with zero downside protection, the exact gap that turned CAPR into a −72% loss. Decide today: (1) let them ride and commit to placing stop-limits the moment any fills, (2) cancel and re-run stock-finder for a fresh read since the setups are now 2 days old, or (3) narrow to your highest-conviction one of the three. Doing nothing is the one option that isn't safe.

🌍 Macro Context — Aug 6, 2026

Buffett Indicator:~230-235% 🔴 ALL-TIME EXTREME
S&P Forward P/E:~25.8x (vs. own long-run avg ~25.4x)
Trend:↑ Rising — was 218% in Q1, 234.3% by late July

Market cap is running well over double annual GDP — historically every reading this high has preceded a multi-year drawdown. Sources still disagree on the exact number (220% to 241% depending on methodology), but all of them sit deep in "danger zone or worse" territory.

For your strategy: you're already at the most defensive position possible — 100% cash. That's not a bad place to be sitting given this macro backdrop; no rush to force a new entry just because cash is idle.

Last historical episodes at this level: 2000 dot-com peak, 2021 COVID bubble peak — see buffett-indicator-history.html.

AppLovin's move was in after-hours trading following its Aug 5 print (as much as -28.7% intraday low); the range reflects after-hours quotes, confirm the regular-session close if you look this up. No other single-name move cleared the 20% bar with a reliable source today — plenty of noise about monthly gainers (IBTA, MOVE, BLZE) but those are 4-week cumulative figures, not single-day moves, so they're excluded per the daily filter.

🏢 Large-cap on deck — next 21 days

Ticker Event Date Setup Direction
NVDA Earnings Aug 26 (20 days out) Guided ~$91B rev ±2%, consensus ~$91.8B; data center +92% YoY; 43 of 47 analysts strong buy 🟢 Bullish

💡 NVDA earnings Aug 26 — near-universal bullish sell-side setup, but bar is already high: guidance is roughly in-line with consensus, not a fresh beat-and-raise setup yet. Say analyze NVDA for the full breakdown closer to the date. No other mega-cap on your radar list (AAPL, MSFT, META, AMZN, GOOG, TSLA, AMD, AVGO, TSM, LLY) has an earnings date inside the next 21 days — MSFT and GOOG already reported in July, AVGO isn't until Sep 2.

⏳ Pending Watchlist

No live watchlist candidates. All 5 entries in portfolio.json's watchlist[] (IQV, CELC, CAPR, VRDN, VERA) are marked ARCHIVE — closed positions kept for the record, not open opportunities. The real pending items right now are the 3 unfilled buy orders in the "Decisions needed" banner above, which live in pending_orders[], not the watchlist. Run stock-finder if you want a fresh discovery pass — it's due to run again this Sunday on its own schedule.

💵 Cash deployment — $542.01 on the books, $216.51 actually free

cash_available shows $542.01, but $325.50 of that is already earmarked: the AXTI, SPXC, and GOOG GTC orders would consume it the moment any of them fill. Treat the real deployable number as ~$216.51, not $540.

No new entry suggestion today. Stacking a 4th order on top of 3 already-unresolved, stop-less ones isn't disciplined position sizing — it's how you end up with 4 fresh names and no downside protection on any of them the same week. Resolve the pending three first (see banner above), then revisit deployment once you know what you're actually holding.

Your call.

🔄 Rotation Suggestions

Not applicable — zero open positions means nothing to rotate out of. This is purely a "what to do with cash and pending orders" day, covered above.

📚 Today you learned

Beat-and-Raise vs. Miss-and-Guide-Down

Today's movers are the textbook version of this. Digital Turbine (APPS) beat EPS by 36% and grew revenue 27% — a clean beat-and-raise, and the stock ripped +48%. AppLovin (APP) missed revenue by just 1.2% and guided next quarter only slightly light — barely a miss by the numbers — yet the stock cratered 20-29%. The lesson: the market doesn't price the beat or miss itself, it prices the change in expectations for every future quarter. A 1% miss that breaks a "this company can do no wrong" narrative (AppLovin's ad-tech growth story) does more damage than a 30% miss on a name nobody expected much from. This is the same mechanic as the whisper-number concept from Day 16 — official consensus is not what's actually priced in.

Also today: Expectations reset — after a violent miss reaction like AppLovin's, the stock's next 1-2 quarters get judged against a much lower bar, which is often when a name becomes an easier beat again.

Research output, not financial advice. Past performance does not guarantee future results. No open positions today, so no live price fetch was required for the portfolio itself. Yahoo Finance JSON API (both hosts) and the stooq fallback all returned HTTP 403 when checked against the pending-order tickers (AXTI, SPXC, GOOG) — their current prices are unavailable this run; check IBKR directly before deciding on those orders.
